title: IBM poised for modest third-quarter beat, says Bank of America
detail:
IBM poised for modest third-quarter beat, says Bank of America
Proactive
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:09 AM PDT 2 min read
IBM
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
IBM poised for modest third-quarter beat, says Bank of America Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America expects International Business Machines Corp (NYSE:IBM), the technology and consulting group, to deliver a modest third-quarter earnings beat on October 21 while keeping its financial 2026 outlook unchanged.

The bank reiterated its 'buy' rating and $280 price target, citing IBM's shift towards higher-margin software, improving profitability and strong free cash flow.

Bank of America forecasts third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion and earnings per share of $2.82, with the potential for a slightly stronger performance from favourable currency movements and profitability.

The bank expects investors to focus on progress in converting delayed deals, signs of a recovery in customer spending and improving growth in Transaction Processing software.

Software growth remains below ideal levels, although Bank of America expects strength in Red Hat (NYSE:RHT)'s OpenShift and Ansible products, alongside continued expansion in the data business following IBM's acquisition of Confluent.

The bank forecasts 4.5% reported software growth for financial 2026, with organic growth, excluding acquisitions, expected to reach 1% for the year as Transaction Processing recovers gradually.

Infrastructure revenue is expected to grow 3% at constant exchange rates in the third quarter, while consulting revenue is forecast to rise 3.6% as growth improves in the second half.

Bank of America describes 2026 as a transitional year for IBM, with a stronger operating performance expected in 2027 as software growth and margins improve.

The bank trimmed its financial 2026 revenue forecast to $70.3 billion from $70.5 billion and its earnings-per-share estimate to $12.40 from $12.45, leaving its price target unchanged at $280.

Its valuation assumes IBM will trade at 19 times the estimated 2027 enterprise value to free cash flow, a measure comparing the company's overall value with the cash it generates after operating costs and capital expenditure.

TORONTO, Oct. 15, 2026 /CNW/ -- Milosevic & Associates PC, a Toronto-based law firm that focuses on civil fraud litigation is investigating Canadian-focused investor claims against Bank of America Corporation (TSX: "BOFA").

On October 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced enforcement actions imposing more than $1.21 billion in penalties against Bank of America ("the Bank"), the second-largest bank in the United States, for violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws.

On December 23, 2024, Bank of America Corporation entered into a Cease and Desist Order with the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency ("OCC") for deficiencies related to the Bank Secrecy Act ("BSA") and sanctions compliance programs relating to anti-money laundering ("AML") issues.

Andrew Morganti, a leading investor lawyer in Toronto, Ontario, for over 15 years and ranked by ISS Top 50 for numerous years, commented, "Investors read and relied upon BOA's statement about cleaning up its AML procedures, even after TD Bank was charged with the same AML deficiency problems a year ago, and now there is an undeniable contraction here:

Bank of America Corporation recently reported,

"Since late 2023, the Corporation has been working with regulators to make changes to its Programs and has already completed significant steps to satisfy requirements of the Consent Order." Form 10-Q (July 31, 2026)

On October 13, 2026, the U.S. regulators reported differently,

"The Bank has not made sufficient progress in addressing its multiple internal control weaknesses since the 2024 Order was issued." Consent Order (October 13, 2026)

On Friday, October 9, 2026, Bank of America's CDRs closed at $27.02 CAD. Upon the release of disclosures about its continued AML violations and an approximate USD $1.3 billion penalty, the market's reaction was immediate by sending the shares down to $25.54 CAD on record volume levels. Under Ontario provincial law, damages are measured from the public correction date and up to ten (10) trading days.

If you purchased Bank of America Corporation's securities in Canada or are a Canadian resident that purchased Bank of America Corporation's securities listed on the NYSE between December 23, 2024 and October 13, 2026, you are welcome to contact us about our investigation at info@mlflitigation.com.

Milosevic & Associates PC is one of the leading Canadian law firms that litigates civil fraud claims. Andrew Morganti, a lawyer in Canada and the United States with a masters in law relating to banking and financial laws, represents Canadian investors in shareholder class actions involving Canadian companies that list their securities on stock exchanges located in Canada, Germany, and the United States. title: Ranking America's 4 Biggest Banks From Best Buy to Worst
detail:
Ranking America's 4 Biggest Banks From Best Buy to Worst
Bram Berkowitz, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:50 AM PDT 6 min read
NVDA
JPM
BAC
C
WFC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Since the Great Recession in 2008, banking has not exactly been the most attractive sector to invest in.

The blow-up in 2008 caused significant reputational damage, which has taken a long time to recover from. Banks have also faced heightened regulations and the constant need to invest in technology, while also trying to ward off competition from fintech companies.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The four largest banks in the U.S. are JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM), Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Citigroup (NYSE: C), and Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC). These money-center banks are essentially now too big to fail. They have also developed scale in many core banking businesses that will be difficult to replicate.

Here they are, ranked from best buy to worst.

Image source: Getty Images.
1. JPMorgan Chase

JPMorgan Chase is the largest bank by assets in the U.S., with nearly $5.1 trillion in assets at the end of the third quarter.

JPMorgan Chase is a best-in-breed large-bank stock, run by CEO Jamie Dimon, long regarded as the industry's best CEO. The bank excels in all facets of banking, including credit card lending, investment banking, trading, payments, commercial lending, and asset and wealth management.

The bank also generates returns on tangible common equity (ROTCE) at the top of its peer group. Management has guided for a long-term ROTCE of 17% through a full economic cycle. But the bank typically generates over a 20% ROTCE, and sometimes much higher.

This is no secret, and, as such, the bank has been awarded a premium valuation based on a price-to-tangible book value (TBV) per-share basis, a common way banks are valued.

JPM Price-to-Tangible Book Value data by YCharts.

So, while JPMorgan Chase may have less near-term appreciation, I still like it best in the long term. It's going to consistently put up industry-leading returns and be the most consistent through the cycle.

2. Citigroup

After years of lagging returns, Jane Fraser took the reins at Citigroup in 2021 and implemented a massive turnaround effort that has paid off.

Fraser sold off international consumer banking divisions that lacked the scale to compete and focused on the bank's best-performing businesses, such as investment banking and payments.

In 2027, the bank will complete the lengthy effort to divest the consumer, small-business, and middle-market banking operations of its large division in Mexico, known as Banamex. Citigroup has already sold nearly half of this division, but will conduct an initial public offering for the rest in 2027, still retaining some ownership.

Bank of America's (BAC) diversified business model continues to grow with the US economy, with its core business of gathering deposits and levering growth with loans poised to lead to strong long-term earnings growth, RBC Capital Markets said in a note.

The bank's Q3 earnings saw contribution from all major business lines, with Consumer Banking revenue rising 4% and adding over 200K net new checking accounts. Global Wealth & Investment Management rose 13%, while Global Banking grew average deposits 6.0% and average loans 8.0%, RBC said Wednesday.

Q3 profit was weighed down, however, by a $1.2 billion non-tax-deductible settlement charge related to deficiencies in the firm's Bank Secrecy Act and Anti-Money Laundering compliance programs, according to the note.

"Given the de-risking of its balance sheet over the last 15 years, we expect BAC to deliver resilient credit quality results over the next 12 months," RBC analysts said.

RBC lowered its price target to $60 from $65 and maintained its outperform rating.

CarMax upgraded to 'buy' by Bank of America as pricing gains drive market share Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America has upgraded CarMax Inc (NYSE:KMX), the US used-car retailer, to 'buy' from 'underperform' and raised its price target to $65 from $50 as improving price competitiveness drives market share gains.

The bank expects enforcement of the Federal Trade Commission's (FTC) price-transparency rules, alongside CarMax's own pricing changes, to support sales growth beyond the initial regulatory boost.

CarMax's comparable used-vehicle sales rose 13% in its second financial quarter, while the wider industry declined 2%, highlighting the company's recent outperformance.

Bank of America said the FTC's campaign, which began in May, should benefit CarMax as dealers face greater pressure to advertise prices that include previously undisclosed fees.

CarMax removed its processing fees in May, and the bank estimates that regulatory changes accounted for half of the improvement in its price competitiveness.

The broker expects the benefits to last as more dealers comply with the rules and customers develop greater trust in CarMax's advertised prices, potentially encouraging repeat purchases.

Bank of America also sees scope for CarMax to reduce prices further through cost savings in vehicle reconditioning and logistics, allowing it to attract more buyers without reducing gross profit per vehicle.

The company has introduced a centralised parts selection tool, shortened its warranty period to 30 days and reduced transfers across the roughly 2 million to 2.5 million vehicles it handles annually.

A review of nearly 500 advertised listings for six popular 2023 vehicle models found CarMax's prices were 0.3% above the market average, compared with 1.2% below average at online rival Carvana and 0.1% below average at franchised dealers.

Bank of America believes cost reductions could give CarMax room to become more price-competitive while maintaining gross profit per vehicle.

The broker also highlighted an opportunity from consumers trading down from new vehicles as affordability pressures persist, with the average new-vehicle transaction price reaching about $50,600 in September.

Higher-income buyers and demand for vehicles aged zero to three years helped lift CarMax's average selling price rose by 6% through changes in the sales mix during the second quarter, while its pricing strategy kept sales to lower-income households stable.

Bank of America identified CarMax's planned November 3 strategic update as a near-term catalyst, with investors expected to look for cost initiatives that can sustain comparable sales growth as the initial pricing and regulatory benefits fade.

Shares of CarMax were trading over 4% higher on Thursday at around $51.85.

title: Bank of America (BAC): Can CashPro Make Earnings More Durable?
detail:
Bank of America (BAC): Can CashPro Make Earnings More Durable?
Jeff Lewis
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:12 AM PDT 4 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) earns interest and fees from lending, payments, wealth management, and capital-markets services for households and businesses. CashPro helps corporate treasurers manage cash and payments. For investors exploring established financial institutions, Bank of America is worth considering among the 10 Most Active Blue Chip Stocks to Buy Right Now.

Dividend Growth in the Banking Sector: Bank of America (BAC)'s Path to Consistent Dividends
Treasury Relationships Can Become Harder to Replace

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) processed 213 million CashPro payments in the first half, up 10%. That growth preceded September's Payments Insights launch. The new tools help clients analyze payment efficiency, cross-border flows, and working capital, including comparisons with peers.

For Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC), established payment records and approval processes can make switching disruptive. Retaining clients longer could spread technology costs over more years and encourage additional deposits, foreign exchange and financing. The test is whether switching costs translate into shareholder returns. Product-specific retention gains and profits remain undisclosed.

Forward Earnings Must Outrun Costs

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) carried an 11x forward P/E against 13x trailing P/E before the latest quarterly reports. Trailing P/E uses past earnings, while forward P/E uses forecast earnings. The 11x valuation looks fair, with higher sustainable earnings needed to support a stronger multiple.

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) has operating drivers that support the earnings-growth outlook. Third-quarter net interest income rose 8% to $16.4 billion as loans and deposits grew and fixed-rate assets repriced. Repurchases also support EPS. These mechanisms help bridge historical and forecast earnings, without establishing a CashPro profit contribution.

Costs complicate that improvement. Third-quarter GAAP EPS was $0.91, versus company-adjusted, non-GAAP EPS of $1.08 excluding a $1.2 billion regulatory settlement. That charge reinforces the need for payment growth to fund effective controls.

The Historical Discount Needs Better Economics

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) carried a 13x forward P/E at year-end 2025, above the 11x pre-results valuation. Uneven capital-markets earnings and higher expenses justify caution about restoring that multiple. A lower valuation becomes attractive when recurring profits strengthen sufficiently to absorb those pressures.

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) reported 10% growth in third-quarter treasury service charges, yet Global Banking revenue was approximately flat at $6.2 billion. Expenses rose 7%, and segment net income fell approximately 5% to $2.0 billion. Stronger treasury fees did not translate into stronger segment earnings.

title: BNY Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Fee Income & NII Growth
detail:
BNY Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Fee Income & NII Growth
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:09 AM PDT 5 min read
BNY
BAC
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation's BNY third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $2.37 per share surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.26. The bottom line increased 24.1% from the year-ago quarter.

Results have primarily benefited from a rise in fee revenues and net interest income (NII). Growth in assets under custody and/or administration (AUC/A) and assets under management (AUM) balances supported the results. However, higher expenses hurt the results to some extent.

Results excluded certain non-recurring items. Considering those, net income applicable to common shareholders (GAAP basis) was $1.61 billion, up 20.1% from the year-ago quarter.

BNY's Fee Revenues & NII Increase

Total revenues increased 11.7% year over year to $5.68 billion. The top line surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.56 billion.

Total fee revenues were $4.08 billion, up 12.1% year over year. Investment services fees increased 15% to $2.97 billion, supported by net new business, higher market values and increased client activity.

Investment management and performance fees rose 2.7% to $803 million. Foreign exchange revenues increased 19.3% to $198 million. Investment and other revenues totaled $175 million, down from $208 million in the prior-year quarter, reflecting the impacts of fixed income and equity trading activity, seed capital results, and the absence of a year-ago disposal gain, partly offset by other investment gains.

NII jumped 15.1% year over year to $1.42 billion. The increase reflected the reinvestment of investment securities at higher yields and balance-sheet growth, partly offset by deposit margin compression.

The net interest margin expanded 12 basis points year over year to 1.43%.

Average loans grew 19.4% from the prior-year quarter to $86.79 billion. Average deposits increased 3.9% to $311.08 billion.

Bank of New York Mellon's Expenses Rise

Total non-interest expenses were $3.49 billion, up 7.8% year over year. Higher revenue-related costs and investments drove the rise, partly offset by efficiency savings.

Despite higher costs, revenue growth outpaced expense growth. This generated 389 basis points of year-over-year operating leverage.

The pre-tax operating margin expanded to 38.5% from 36.4% a year earlier.

BNY's Asset Balances Expand

AUC/A were $63.4 trillion as of Sept. 30, 2026, up 9.7% year over year. The increase reflected higher market values, net client inflows and net new business, partly offset by the unfavorable impact of a stronger U.S. dollar.

AUM increased 2.1% to $2.19 trillion. Higher market values supported the balance, though cumulative net outflows and unfavorable currency movements were headwinds.
